rtt_step_pattern.observation: RTTs in this DROP1_OUT run fall on levels about 20 ms apart: {'26 ms': 80, '46 ms': 77, '66 ms': 79, '86 ms': 84, '106 ms': 84, '126 ms': 4, '146 ms': 4, '166 ms': 1, '246 ms': 1, '346 ms': 1} (counts of the 415 selected values by nearest level). The P95 of 105.897 ms is on the 106 ms level. The same pattern is present in the 13 other runs with 415 selected values: concentration R 0.834 to 0.998, share within 3 ms of the ladder 0.870 to 1.000; this run has R 0.888 and share 0.940.
rtt_step_pattern.measure: Circular concentration of RTT modulo 20 ms (R: 0 = even, 1 = all on one phase) and the share of values within 3 ms of the phase centre (a flat spread would give about 0.30).
rtt_step_pattern.status: Observation only. The cause is not established; an earlier working suspicion is system timing granularity. It is kept as a flag so the thesis analysis does not read the steps as network effects.

server_log_loss_retransmit_comparison.text: Server log comparison with HBPSN-10: neither server log (nor the serial log) contains any loss or retransmission counter or message, so the number of lost or retransmitted messages is not recorded and is not estimated here. What the logs show: in both runs 441 RECEIVED lines match the 441 RTT records, one QUIC CONNECTED line, no sequence gap, no connection error and an empty stderr. Both logs hold one "QUIC CLOSED | code=1 | Idle timeout" line at line 22, after RECEIVED seq 9 and before seq 10 (between 53 s and 58 s of board uptime), while the connection continues to seq 441; a QUIC CLOSED line at line 22 is also in the server logs of HBPSN-01, 05, 12, 13 and 15 (HBPSN-03 and 08, the failed-startup attempts, differ). Cause not established and not asserted. These files do not show whether any packet was dropped or retransmitted: the server log records application messages only, and the number of packets Clumsy dropped is not recorded in them.
